# `Db.Unsafe`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Db.Unsafe — the raw-SQL and untyped-column-read escape hatches for
`Ipe.Db`.

This submodule is the one home for the database members that bypass a
security or type invariant of the safe default. Importing it discloses the
`unsafe` capability program-wide, so a dependency's raw-SQL or untyped-read
sink is visible before the program runs.

Every member is a point-free `Kernel.kernel "Db_<member>"` / `"Sql_<member>"`
alias to a retained runtime kernel; only the surface home moved here from
`Ipe.Db` / `Ipe.Db.Sql`. The kernels, their registry keys, and their runtime
behaviour are unchanged.

Two invariants are hatched here:

  * SQL-injection axis — `unsafeExecRaw` and `unsafeQuery` issue verbatim,
    caller-authored SQL text. No validator makes arbitrary SQL safe; the safe
    default is `Db.exec` / `Db.queryDecode` with parameterised binds and the
    `Sql.*` combinators over a validated `SqlFragment`. `unsafeFragment` mints
    a `SqlFragment` from an unchecked string, deliberately skipping the
    `Sql.column` identifier validation — the caller asserts the fragment is a
    safe SQL identifier.

  * Type-safety axis — the `unsafeGet*` family reads a column by string key
    with no decode proof, bypassing the typed `Db.queryDecode` row codec. No
    SQL is issued, so there is no injection risk; the caller asserts the
    column's runtime type matches the read.

## `unsafeExecRaw`

```ipe
unsafeExecRaw : Db -> String -> Task Error Int
```

`unsafeExecRaw conn sql` — run verbatim, caller-authored SQL. No validator
runs; the caller owns the injection invariant. Parameterised `Db.exec` is the
safe default.

## `unsafeQuery`

```ipe
unsafeQuery : Db -> String -> List SqlValue -> Task Error (List (Dict String String))
```

`unsafeQuery conn sql binds` — the query TEXT is caller-authored verbatim;
only the `binds` are parameterised. `Db.queryDecode` with `Sql.*` is the safe
default.

## `unsafeGetString`

```ipe
unsafeGetString : String -> Dict String String -> String
```

`unsafeGetString key row` — read column `key` as a `String`, bypassing the
typed row codec. The caller asserts the column holds a string.

## `unsafeGetInt`

```ipe
unsafeGetInt : String -> Dict String String -> Int
```

`unsafeGetInt key row` — read column `key` as an `Int`, bypassing the typed
row codec. The caller asserts the column holds an integer.

## `unsafeGetBool`

```ipe
unsafeGetBool : String -> Dict String String -> Bool
```

`unsafeGetBool key row` — read column `key` as a `Bool`, bypassing the typed
row codec. The caller asserts the column holds a boolean.

## `unsafeGetField`

```ipe
unsafeGetField : String -> Dict String String -> String
```

`unsafeGetField key row` — read column `key` as an untyped string field,
bypassing the typed row codec. The caller asserts the column's type.

## `unsafeFragment`

```ipe
unsafeFragment : String -> SqlFragment
```

`unsafeFragment s` — mint a `SqlFragment` from `s` verbatim, WITHOUT the
`Sql.column` identifier validation. The anti-`Sql.column`: the parse is
skipped by caller assertion. The caller asserts `s` is a safe SQL identifier
or fragment; `Sql.column` is the safe, validated default.

## `unsafeExecRawOn`

```ipe
unsafeExecRawOn : Connection ReadWrite -> String -> Task Error Int
```

`unsafeExecRawOn conn sql` — run verbatim, caller-authored SQL against an
external connection. Requires a `Connection ReadWrite`, so a `Connection
ReadOnly` from `Db.Dsn.open` cannot reach it (a compile error, not a runtime
check). The caller owns the injection invariant; `sql` is issued verbatim.
`Connection`/`ReadWrite` are reserved types — this hatch pulls in no other
module, so a raw-SQL program stays lean.
